claim: The 60s idle timeout rests on an undocumented, unverified liveness contract: the SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS comment records no basis for 60s and the invariant (watchdog runs below the SSE parser so keepalive lines reset the timer; every endpoint must emit data/keepalives more often than 60s) is uncaptured.

claim: The timeout-signaling mechanism (destroy -> read resolves {done:true} -> timedOut flag -> post-loop throw) is entirely undocumented; a timed-out stream exits the loop through the same `if (result.done) break` as clean EOF, so a maintainer could 'simplify' the post-loop throw and break the timeout path.
raw: The design hinges on a non-obvious WHATWG Streams fact: `stream.destroy()` -> `reader.cancel()` **resolves** the in-flight `read()` with `{ done: true }` - it does not reject. A timed-out stream is therefore indistinguishable inside the loop from a normally completed one
